title: Dip minima recur more at short gaps than long gaps in 39 TESS complex periodic variable stars
abstract: We test whether individual dip minima return near the same spot-relative phases in released TESS complex periodic variable measurements. We compare sets of minima without fitting a whole-template shift. An exact rotation control keeps dip counts and spacings. In 39 stars with both gaps below 60 days and gaps of at least 400 days, the short-minus-long excess match fraction is 0.293 (95% star-bootstrap interval 0.185 to 0.402), at a tolerance of 0.05 cycles. No one of 5,000 within-star epoch-order permutations reaches this contrast (Monte Carlo p = 0.00020). This test uses all pairs, without a shape-quality cut, and keeps each star's measured patterns and fixed phase preferences. In source-quality short-gap pairs, the site-match excess is 0.347 (0.271 to 0.421). It remains 0.153 (0.063 to 0.247) in 86 pairs from 27 stars with moderate dip-shape agreement. The result supports short-term memory of detectable dip sites. It does not identify surviving material or set a clump lifetime. Limits include source decomposition, a changing spot reference, detection selection and no raw-cadence injection calibration for this statistic. Code, exact source hashes, aggregate results and repeat steps are included. Record-level inputs remain in the cited source.
